summary: Credential-proxy redirect chain observed after employee submitted external form
description:
Issue summary: Employee A (redacted) reported an unusual redirect after completing an external vendor feedback form. Instead of returning to the vendor's confirmation page, the browser briefly navigated to a shortened redirect URI and then to a domain that proxies an OAuth authorization prompt. Impact: Potential credential-probing or token interception attempt; several other employees received the same form link via an external mailing list. No confirmed token theft, but multiple anomalous SSO approval prompts were logged. Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 08:14 UTC: Employee A submits external form (vendor X).
- 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC: Browser redirect observed to short.link/rt7 -> redirector.example.com/proxy -> auth-proxy.biz/oauth?client_id=...
- 2026-03-10 08:16 UTC: Employee reports unexpected SSO approval prompt; did not approve.
- 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC: Support triage ticket created.
- 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: SRE added temporary WAF rule blocking redirector.example.com.
Initial detection: Report from employee + correlating Web Proxy logs showed same redirect chain for 6 employees over 48 hours. Steps to reproduce: 1) Click vendor X form link from the external mailing list; 2) Observe redirect chain in browser devtools; 3) If SSO session exists, an approval prompt presented from auth-proxy.biz. Logs and evidence:
- Web Proxy logs (prod/us-west): proxy-redir-logs-2026-03-10.gz (link: https://logs.redwood.internal/web/2026-03-10/proxy-redir-logs)
- CAS audit: many 'consent_required' events with client_id matching unknown proxy (client_id: proxy-client-92)
- Endpoint telemetry: browser extension flagged redirect to auth-proxy.biz on 6 hosts
Hypothesis: External form vendor's redirector was either compromised or abused to chain to a credential-proxy domain that attempts to present an OAuth consent screen to hijack SSO tokens or trick users into consenting to permissions. No backend token exchange observed in logs. Next steps: 1) Block redirector and auth-proxy.biz at perimeter/WAF and update email filters; 2) Identify all employees who clicked the link and confirm they did not approve prompts; 3) Rotate any short-lived tokens if approval was mistakenly given; 4) Contact vendor X to request takedown and forensic logs; 5) Run a targeted scan for similar redirector domains in recent inbound emails; 6) Create an incident advisory to employees with guidance. Business impact: Medium - potential for lateral access if a user consented. Mitigation in place: temporary perimeter blocks and email deletion request to vendor mailing list.
Notes: No successful OAuth token exchange found in authorization logs; CAS did not show token issuance for proxy-client-92. We treated as Sev1 due to user-facing SSO prompts and multiple recipients.
Next update planned: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC or sooner if new findings.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open external vendor X form link received via mailing list. 2) Watch for redirect chain short.link -> redirector.example.com -> auth-proxy.biz. 3) If already logged into SSO, observe consent prompt from unfamiliar client. 4) Do not grant consent; report to security@redwood.com.
investigation_notes: Checked CAS audit logs for token issuance: none found for proxy-client-92.
Correlated web-proxy logs show 6 hosts in us-west contacted redirector.example.com between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10.
Endpoint telemetry captured suspicious JavaScript injection on vendor form page on a single host; vendor likely compromised.
WAF rule deployed at 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC to block auth-proxy.biz and redirector.example.com.
mitigation_actions: Temporary WAF block for auth-proxy.biz and redirector.example.com applied.
Email filter rule created to quarantine messages containing short.link and vendor X forms.
Targeted message sent to affected employees with instructions not to approve prompts and to clear browser sessions.
Vendor X contacted requesting immediate takedown and logs; security contact provided.
SSO client registry scanned; unknown client 'proxy-client-92' flagged and disabled pending further investigation.
resolution: Ongoing - containment measures applied; vendor engagement in progress. No tokens confirmed exfiltrated as of 2026-03-12.
